what_it_does: Twilio's transactional and marketing email delivery service.
auth_notes: v3 API uses an API key (created in Settings > API Keys, scoped by permissions) sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'. Basic auth not documented on the auth page.
access_notes: Self-serve signup gives a 60-day free trial (up to 100 emails/day) per a Twilio developer blog; no permanent free tier mentioned. Sending also needs a verified sender/domain.
api_notes: v3 REST API: mail send, API keys and permissions, contacts/marketing, templates, stats, suppressions, sender authentication, subusers, webhooks.
human_needed: verify a sender identity/domain before sending
round2_change: Fully researched from scratch: API key/Bearer auth, 60-day trial access, community MCP; was entirely unknown.

what_it_does: Open-source or Adobe-licensed ecommerce platform with REST/GraphQL/SOAP web APIs.
auth_notes: Admin/customer token-based (Bearer) auth; Integration credentials using OAuth 1.0a (listed as 'other'/OAuth-style); session cookie auth for storefront JS. Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service/SaaS uses separate IMS-based REST auth. Every store has its own base URL.
access_notes: Adobe describes Magento Open Source as 'a free eCommerce platform' that can be downloaded and self-hosted, so a developer can stand up a test store and create an integration/token alone. Adobe Commerce (PaaS/SaaS) is a paid licensed product.
api_notes: REST, SOAP and GraphQL web APIs covering catalog, orders, customers, inventory, carts, CMS; resources defined per module in webapi.xml.
main_blocker: per-store self-hosted base URL; store admin must create integration/token
human_needed: store admin creates integration or admin token for each store
notes: Adobe's own MCP servers (App Builder MCP, Dropins MCP) are developer tooling, not store-data connectors, so store-data MCP is community (Marketplace/Packagist modules such as angeo/module-mcp-server, scandiweb write-up). OAuth 1.0a integrations mapped to OAuth2+other since OAuth1 is not an allowed value.
round2_change: Confirmed Magento Open Source is free to self-host (access now self-serve-free) and downgraded MCP from official to community since Adobe's MCPs are dev tooling only.

what_it_does: Embeddable online store builder by Lightspeed for adding shops to sites.
auth_notes: REST API uses OAuth 2.0 (simplified for single-store custom apps); custom apps created in the store admin's app dashboard get access tokens directly; public App Market apps use the OAuth flow.
access_notes: Docs state 'Only stores on paid plans can access API.' Ecwid support can grant a free paid-plan upgrade for test stores/app development on request by email.
api_notes: Store profile, orders, abandoned carts, products/variations/reviews, customers and groups, categories, discounts/coupons, payment/shipping settings; 600 req/min per token.
human_needed: subscribe to a paid Ecwid plan or email support for a free dev-store upgrade
notes: No official Ecwid/Lightspeed MCP found; Zapier (third-party hosted) and other aggregators offer Ecwid MCP actions.
round2_change: Fully researched: OAuth2 REST API, paid plan required (free dev upgrade on request), third-party MCP; was entirely unknown.

what_it_does: Platform for creators to sell digital products and memberships.
auth_notes: Create an application in Settings > Advanced; generate a personal access token (non-expiring) for own account, or use OAuth 2.0 auth-code flow (client_id/secret, refresh tokens) for other accounts. Token sent as Bearer.
access_notes: Any Gumroad account can create an application and token; no plan requirement mentioned.
api_notes: v2 API at api.gumroad.com: user, products, sales (refund/ship), licenses, subscribers, offer codes, variants, custom fields, payouts, resource subscriptions (webhooks).
notes: Endpoint list comes from the Mintlify-hosted docs of Gumroad's open-source repo (antiwork/gumroad). Community MCPs also exist (rmarescu/gumroad-mcp).
round2_change: Fully researched: OAuth2/personal token, free self-serve, moderate REST API, official OAuth MCP; was entirely unknown.

what_it_does: Amazon API for sellers and vendors to manage listings, orders and fulfillment.
auth_notes: Login with Amazon (LWA), Amazon's OAuth 2.0: private apps self-authorize (refresh token) in draft; public apps use Appstore or website authorization workflows.
access_notes: Must register as an SP-API developer in the Solution Provider Portal: private seller apps need a Professional selling account (paid) and primary account user; submit developer profile with security-control answers and request each role (restricted roles need qualification). Public developers must list in the Appstore. Planned $1,400/yr + GET-call fees were delayed and then reported cancelled (Amazon email, 12 May 2026).
api_notes: Dozens of SP-API sections: orders, listings, catalog, feeds, reports, FBA inventory/fulfillment, finances, notifications, pricing, vendor APIs; access gated by role.
main_blocker: developer registration and role approval; Professional seller account
human_needed: register in Solution Provider Portal, pass developer profile review and request roles
notes: Official MCP is from amzn/selling-partner-agentic-toolkit (Seller Central OAuth). Fee status from developer.amazonservices.com/spp-announcement (delayed) and novadata.io (cancelled), the latter a third-party report.
round2_change: Fully researched: LWA OAuth2, Professional account + developer/role approval gate, official Amazon MCP, fee cancellation noted; was entirely unknown.

what_it_does: Checkout, payments and financing platform for high-ticket digital businesses.
auth_notes: No public API auth docs found. Third-party builder (Emergent) mentions 'API credentials' and a FanBasis Checkout SDK without detail; Zapier app uses account connection.
access_notes: fanbasis.com mentions '7000+ App Integrations' (via Zapier) but no API, developer docs or API keys; access path otherwise is demo call or account signup.
api_notes: Only Zapier triggers/actions (new sale, failed payment, manual transactions, cancellations, disputes, member joins) found; no documented REST API.
human_needed: ask FanBasis whether private API credentials/docs exist
notes: Low confidence: an undocumented or partner-only API may exist (Emergent references API credentials); nothing public was found. Primary_auth 'other' used because no auth is documented.
round2_change: Identified the product (high-ticket checkout platform) and found no public API, only Zapier; verdict now blocked.

what_it_does: B2B contact and company enrichment, search and email verification via waterfall providers.
auth_notes: API key issued after signup, sent in x-api-key header (401 missing, 403 invalid).
access_notes: Prepaid credit top-up model, billed per successful result; no free trial found; rates vary by endpoint/volume and are quoted after a benchmark. Signup reportedly yields an API key, but whether signup is fully self-serve vs sales-led is not confirmed (waterfall.io/pricing not fetchable).
api_notes: ~23 async launch-then-retrieve endpoints: contact/company/phone enrichment, prospect search, job change, email verify, /v2/account usage; 50 req/min default.
main_blocker: paid credits required; no free trial confirmed
human_needed: sign up and buy credits (possibly after sales benchmark)
notes: All evidence third-party (Leadsforge/Salesforge reviews, Cargo and withone connector docs); official site/docs were not reachable. Agent skills on GitHub reported but no MCP server found.
round2_change: Access model resolved from unknown to paid-plan (prepaid credits, no trial found), still third-party sourced.

auth_notes: Atlas Administration API: service-account OAuth2 client credentials -> Bearer token, or legacy programmatic API keys via HTTP Digest ('other'). Org Owner creates them; optional IP access list. Data access uses DB user + connection string.
access_notes: Self-serve Atlas signup with free tier cluster; Admin API credentials created by the org owner without sales. Data API/HTTPS endpoints reached end-of-life in September 2025, so document CRUD needs drivers (or the MCP server).
api_notes: Admin API v2 (cloud.mongodb.com/api/atlas/v2) for projects, clusters, users, access lists, backups, alerts. No REST data plane since Data API EOL; data ops via drivers.
notes: Resolved the round-1 contradiction in favour of 'ready': credentials are fully self-serve and the Admin API is a documented REST API. Data-plane needing a driver is an implementation detail (the official MCP already uses a connection string), not an access blocker, so main_blocker is 'none'.
round2_change: Fixed contradiction: kept buildability 'ready' and set main_blocker to 'none'; added Data API EOL (Sept 2025) evidence.

what_it_does: Payment gateway product, reportedly NMI-powered; vendor not identifiable.
auth_notes: No docs for a 'Paygent Connect' product exist publicly. If it is an NMI white-label, NMI uses security/API keys created in the gateway (partners can create merchant keys) - inference only.
access_notes: Searches for 'Paygent Connect' return no matching product page. Found only: Paygent (Japan) via IXOPAY adapters needing Paygent-issued merchant ID/certificate, and NMI's generic gateway (docs.nmi.com, sandbox and partner APIs, no Paygent mention).
api_notes: No public Paygent Connect API. Underlying NMI gateway has public REST docs and sandbox that could work for a merchant on an NMI reseller gateway (unconfirmed).
main_blocker: no public API / product not identifiable
human_needed: confirm vendor identity and obtain merchant gateway credentials from the reseller
notes: If the reseller confirms it is an NMI white-label, re-scope as the NMI toolkit (API/security key auth, merchant-gated). 'other' auth used because no Paygent auth is documented.
round2_change: Re-searched; still no product found, so access set to no-public-api (was unknown) and verdict stays blocked.

what_it_does: Forensic FX audit detecting hidden bank markups on cross-border payments.
auth_notes: Free MCP tools (check_fx_rate, audit_transaction 3/month per IP, compare_fx_sources) need no auth; full_forensic_report needs a Bearer token/API key. Another listing says an optional IPAYX_API_KEY (free from ipayx.ai) enables live provider quotes. How to obtain keys not documented.
access_notes: Core tools are unauthenticated and free; paid per-report tool price not listed. Publisher iPAYX-Technologies (11850091 Canada Inc.). Dashboard at app.ipayx.ai; no first-party API docs verified.
api_notes: Only MCP surfaces found (hosted streamable-HTTP worker and an npm stdio package) with 3-4 tools; no REST reference.
main_blocker: no documented public REST API; only small MCP surface
human_needed: obtain API key for paid report tool
notes: Hosted endpoint is https://wild-bird-a412.ybolduc.workers.dev/mcp. Tool names differ between listings (two variants), suggesting evolving/duplicated servers. All evidence from MCP directories; ipayx.ai not fetched.
round2_change: Confirmed publisher repo (iPAYX-Technologies/mcp-fx-audit) and second stdio variant; verdict unchanged.

what_it_does: Cloud accounting for small businesses: invoicing, bank reconciliation, payroll.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0 auth code/PKCE for multi-tenant apps; Custom Connections use client credentials for a single organisation.
access_notes: New apps default to the free Starter tier (no payment method, 5 connections, 1,000 calls/day/org). Tiers from 2 Mar 2026: Core A$35/50 conns, Plus A$245/1,000, Advanced A$1,445/10,000, Enterprise POA; >5 connections needs payment and app certification. Developer Terms ban using API data to train AI/ML models.
api_notes: Accounting (contacts, invoices, payments, bank transactions, journals, reports, items, tax), Payroll, Assets, Projects, Files APIs; egress metered on paid tiers.
main_blocker: app certification and paid tier beyond 5 connections
human_needed: pass Xero app certification and add billing to scale past 5 connections
notes: Pricing page also mentions an official Remote MCP server usable with a demo org on Starter. Policy FAQ: https://developer.xero.com/faq/pricing-and-policy-updates.
round2_change: Verified 2026 tiered pricing with free Starter tier (access now self-serve-free) and set blocker to certification/paid tier for scale.

what_it_does: Corporate cards, expense management and business banking.
auth_notes: Account/card admins create scoped user tokens in Settings > Developer after accepting the Developer API agreement (expire after 90 days unused). Partner OAuth2 client ID/secret issued by contacting Brex developer support. MCP uses OAuth (accounts-api.brex.com).
access_notes: Requires a Brex customer account; an account/card admin must accept the developer API agreement and create tokens. No sandbox: production only (api.brex.com). Partner OAuth credentials only via Brex developer support.
api_notes: Team/users, cards and limits, expenses, transactions, payments, budgets/spend limits, accounting, travel, bills/vendors; MCP exposes ~41 tools.
main_blocker: Brex customer account required; no sandbox; partner OAuth via support
human_needed: Brex admin accepts API agreement and issues token, or request partner OAuth credentials
notes: MCP is beta and must be enabled under Settings > Beta features.
round2_change: Verified from official docs: admin tokens + partner OAuth via support, production-only, official MCP at api.brex.com/mcp.

what_it_does: Corporate cards, spend management, bill pay and accounting automation.
auth_notes: OAuth 2.0: client credentials for own business, authorization code + refresh for third-party apps; apps created in the Ramp Developer Console. Some scopes are partner-only.
access_notes: Requires a Ramp customer account with admin access to create a developer app; business-wide apps need Admin/Business Owner approval. Sandbox (demo.ramp.com) is by request, not self-serve.
api_notes: Developer API for transactions, cards, users, reimbursements, bills, vendors, accounting sync, etc.; separate sandbox and production environments.
main_blocker: Ramp customer admin account required; sandbox by request
human_needed: Ramp admin creates/approves app or request sandbox access
notes: Breadth of resources inferred from docs index; getting-started page only showed Transactions. Sandbox MCP at https://demo-mcp.ramp.com/mcp; custom MCP clients need redirect URI allowlisting.
round2_change: Verified from official docs: OAuth2 grants, admin-gated customer access, sandbox on request, official MCP at mcp.ramp.com.

what_it_does: Private capital market data on companies, deals, investors and funds.
auth_notes: PitchBook team provisions the connection via API key or authentication token.
access_notes: API is separate from the platform and needs a standalone contract via the Direct Data team; existing clients request via My PitchBook > Plugins & Apps. No free/trial access.
api_notes: Relational endpoints across companies, deals/financings, investors, funds, people, incl. VC exit predictor data; full list in Endpoints Overview doc.
notes: Morningstar (PitchBook parent) investor Q&A confirms premium PitchBook MCP connectors in Claude/ChatGPT for paying subscribers, plus a direct MCP being piloted; no public MCP URL found, so mcp_url is null. api_breadth 'broad' inferred from 'variety of relational endpoints'.
round2_change: Verified sales-contract access from PitchBook help page and found official (subscriber-only) MCP connectors.

what_it_does: AI meeting assistant that records, transcribes and summarizes conversations.
auth_notes: Official MCP (mcp.otter.ai/mcp) uses OAuth sign-in. Public REST API uses user-created API keys (Integrations > Developer > Create key, max 2/user) sent as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>'.
access_notes: Otter's help pages describe self-serve key creation and MCP OAuth without stating plan limits; only 'Enterprise plan users are limited to 10 requests/second' is mentioned, and a third-party guide claims the REST API is Enterprise-only. In Claude/ChatGPT workspaces an admin must add the connector; Cursor users add it themselves.
api_notes: Public API: channels, channel members, conversations (create from file URL, list, get with transcript/summary/action items, audio), workspace. MCP: get_user_info, search, fetch.
main_blocker: plan eligibility unconfirmed (REST possibly Enterprise-only); narrow API
human_needed: Otter user authorizes OAuth; confirm plan eligibility with Otter support
notes: Access set to self-serve-free as the most defensible reading of official pages (no plan gate stated, the MCP help page defers plan eligibility to support); may be paid-plan/Enterprise in practice.
round2_change: Found Otter's own help pages for MCP and Public API; access changed from admin-approval to self-serve-free (plan gate unconfirmed).

what_it_does: Open-source CLI rendering Mermaid diagram definitions to SVG, PNG or PDF.
auth_notes: Local open-source tool (mmdc, npm @mermaid-js/mermaid-cli); no credentials.
access_notes: Free MIT package; runs locally via Node/Puppeteer or Docker. No hosted service from the CLI project.
api_notes: One function: render .mmd/markdown to SVG/PNG/PDF with theme/config options; Node API but no HTTP API.
main_blocker: No hosted API: CLI must be wrapped in a sandboxed runtime (Node + headless Chromium)
notes: Community MCP @peng-shawn/mermaid-mcp-server (Puppeteer, one 'generate' tool); others: hustcc/mcp-mermaid, tci-nebula/mermaid-mcp. Mermaid Chart offers a hosted OAuth MCP (https://mcp.mermaid.ai/mcp) for validate/render, but it is a separate commercial product, not the CLI. Changed to ready-with-friction because the runtime requirement is a real build blocker.
round2_change: Fixed ready-vs-blocker contradiction: CLI-only tool, wrappable in a sandbox -> ready-with-friction (same ruling as Sherlock, see human review).
